analysis: Changed behavior: SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift (head 119-177) refactors maxStageBytes/maxStageMillis into private configured* parsers. The general defaults are unchanged: 1 GiB and 1000 ms. The PR adds completeCheckpointMaxStageBytes/Millis (head 161-177). On Macs with at least 96 GiB of physical memory (line 157), these default to 3 GiB and 2500 ms (lines 158-159). Explicit env settings still win, and invalid settings fall back to the memory-based default. TTL, HMAC naming, AAD/crypto, the kill switch and the disk/endurance guards are untouched, so the T-041 (a)-(d) posture is unchanged. The only visible caller is the live qualification test ModelCheckpointStorageArtifacts.swift:36. It now uses the new cap as maximumPlaintextBytes for SSDBlockStore.readStreaming. The new unit tests (SSDCompleteCheckpointStageCapTests.swift) check thresholds and precedence. Relevant threats are T-041(e) and its 'no persistent memory carve' mitigation, which bounds transient staging RAM via GlobalKVCacheBudget reservations; TB-007 availability is also relevant. Tripling the per-adoption staged bytes and the pre-submit stage time on large-memory hosts widens transient RAM and TTFT-deadline exposure. Production consumers are not supplied: SSDPrefixCache / SSDBlockStore complete-checkpoint staging, and the write-behind queue cap. Per policy line 237, that queue cap is max(writeQueueMaxBytes, maxStageBytes+slack). The next pass should verify four things: 1) production staging of complete checkpoints still takes a GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation sized to the larger staged bytes, and releases it on all paths; 2) the write-behind byte cap and the donation gate are not silently derived from the new larger cap, which would widen the at-rest surface or host RAM without review; 3) readStreaming still enforces maximumPlaintextBytes before allocation, so hostile or controller-replayed files on external volumes cannot force 3 GiB allocations; 4) the threat model or docs note the memory-tiered staging cap. No concrete regression is evident from the supplied source.
